included.novelty_implication: Medical abstention is an established benchmark topic; DAL cannot claim novelty for an abstain option or for medical abstention evaluation.
included.relationship_to_dal: Introduces MedQAbstain and reports systematic LLM overcommitment under medical uncertainty. DAL native-abstention rows derive from MedQAbstain under DAL's own frozen protocol.
included.title: LLMs (Almost) Never Abstain Under Medical Uncertainty

included.novelty_implication: Closes any claim that DAL is first to evaluate abstention for discrete medical action selection.
included.relationship_to_dal: MedAbstain: unified abstention benchmark and protocol for medical MCQA with conformal prediction, perturbations, and explicit abstention options; frames discrete choice as generalizing to agentic action selection.
included.title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty

included.novelty_implication: General abstention benchmarking exists; DAL contributes no new abstention benchmark.
included.relationship_to_dal: AbstentionBench: large-scale abstention benchmark across 20 datasets showing reasoning LLMs fail on unanswerable questions.
included.title: AbstentionBench: Reasoning LLMs Fail on Unanswerable Questions

included.novelty_implication: Closes novelty for a clinical uncertainty/abstention governance layer; the DAL name (Decision Assurance Layer) must not imply a first such layer.
included.relationship_to_dal: MedBayes-Lite: retraining-free uncertainty governance layer combining MC dropout, calibration, and confidence-guided abstention; reports that it does not improve risk-coverage ranking.
included.title: MedBayes-Lite: A Clinical Uncertainty Governance Layer for Risk-Aware Medical Decision Support

included.novelty_implication: Decision-theoretic abstention framing is established; DAL must cite it and not present that framing as new.
included.relationship_to_dal: Peer-reviewed review and decision-theoretic framing of healthcare LLM abstention.
included.title: When silence is safer: a review and decision-theoretic framework for LLM abstention in healthcare

included.novelty_implication: Missing-information overconfidence is documented; the DAL native unsafe-commit pathology is consistent with, not novel relative to, this literature.
included.relationship_to_dal: Behavioral analysis of LLM overconfidence under missing clinical information.
included.title: When Confidence Fails: Overconfidence in LLMs under Uncertainty and Missing Clinical Information

included.novelty_implication: Selective prediction on medical text is established prior work.
included.relationship_to_dal: Uncertainty-aware abstention for diagnosis from medical texts using selective prediction.
included.title: Uncertainty-aware abstention in medical diagnosis based on medical texts

included.novelty_implication: Further prior clinical abstention work; no DAL abstention-method novelty.
included.relationship_to_dal: KnowGuard: knowledge-driven abstention for multi-round clinical reasoning.
included.title: KnowGuard: Knowledge-Driven Abstention for Multi-Round Clinical Reasoning

included.novelty_implication: Agent-level when-not-to-act evaluation exists; DAL taglines must not imply a first agentic abstention evaluation.

included.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?

included.novelty_implication: Sequential agentic abstention is defined elsewhere; DAL evaluates only single-decision abstention.
included.relationship_to_dal: Agentic Abstention: sequential stop-versus-act decision problem for LLM agents.
included.title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?

included.novelty_implication: Methodology reference for DAL risk-coverage reporting; supports reporting AURC and fixed-coverage risk descriptively.
included.relationship_to_dal: Methodological requirements for multi-threshold selective-classification metrics such as AURC variants, with clinical motivation.
included.title: Overcoming Common Flaws in the Evaluation of Selective Classification Systems

included.novelty_implication: Methodology reference; DAL AURC values are finite-sample descriptive estimates.
included.relationship_to_dal: Population AURC characterization and finite-sample estimation rates.
included.title: A Novel Characterization of the Population Area Under the Risk Coverage Curve (AURC) and Rates of Finite Sample Estimators

included.novelty_implication: DAL makes no FHIR performance claim; the blocked result is reported as blocked.

included.title: FHIR-AgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Realistic Interoperable EHR Question Answering

included.novelty_implication: No end-to-end agent claim is possible for DAL.

included.novelty_implication: Healthcare agent evaluation suites exist at much larger scope; DAL is not positioned as an agent benchmark.

included.title: HealthAgentBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite of Realistic Agentic Healthcare Environments for Challenging Frontier AI Agents

included.novelty_implication: FHIR QA benchmarking is active; no DAL FHIR novelty claim.
included.relationship_to_dal: FHIRPath-QA: executable patient-specific QA over FHIR records.
included.title: FHIRPath-QA: Executable Question Answering over FHIR Electronic Health Records

included.novelty_implication: Concurrent FHIR-AgentBench method work; DAL has no comparable FHIR result.

included.novelty_implication: Supports the DAL rule that serialization-only effects cannot carry FHIR capability claims.

included.novelty_implication: Calibrated deferral with evidence grounding in EHR settings exists; DAL cannot claim to be first to combine them.

included.title: CliniCARE-Bench: Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR

included.novelty_implication: Evidence verification is established; DAL has no qualified real-data evidence-intervention result and therefore no grounding claim.
included.relationship_to_dal: Guideline-verified stepwise process rewards; not architecturally equivalent to DAL.
included.title: Med-PRM: Medical Reasoning Models with Stepwise, Guideline-verified Process Rewards

included.novelty_implication: Evidence-verified biomedical QA exists; no DAL grounding claim.
included.relationship_to_dal: MedTrust-RAG: evidence verification and trust alignment for biomedical QA.
included.title: MedTrust-RAG: Evidence Verification and Trust Alignment for Biomedical Question Answering

included.novelty_implication: Small-model evidence attribution exists; no DAL attribution claim.
included.relationship_to_dal: Med-V1: small models for zero-shot biomedical evidence attribution.
included.title: Med-V1: Small Language Models for Zero-shot and Scalable Biomedical Evidence Attribution

included.novelty_implication: Evidence-grounded clinical QA benchmarks exist.

included.title: EHRNote-ChatQA: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multi-Turn Clinical Question Answering over Longitudinal Discharge Summaries

included.novelty_implication: Medical calibration benchmarking is established; DAL reports ECE descriptively only.
included.relationship_to_dal: Benchmark of LLM uncertainty and calibration across clinical specialties and question types.
included.title: Mind the Gap: Benchmarking LLM Uncertainty and Calibration with Specialty-Aware Clinical QA and Reasoning-Based Behavioural Features

included.novelty_implication: Confidence-calibration measurement in medical QA is not novel.

included.title: Calibration of Self-Reported Confidence and Accuracy of Large Language Models in Medical Question Answering

included.novelty_implication: Closes any claim that DAL is the first typed-decision or System-One evaluation in medicine or on PubMedQA.

included.novelty_implication: Coherence testing exists; DAL does not evaluate coherence.

included.title: Beyond Calibration: Do a Typed-Decision Model's Probabilities Obey the Probability Axioms?

included.novelty_implication: Selective-automation evaluation of System-One models exists; supports reporting DAL failure concentrations such as the unsafe-commit pathology rather than aggregates only.

included.novelty_implication: Closes any claim that DAL is the first pre-registered typed-decision evaluation.

included.novelty_implication: Evidence-ledger governance framing exists; no first-evidence-ledger claim.

included.novelty_implication: Claim-to-evidence provenance constraints exist in agent reasoning; DAL claim binding is not novel in principle.

included.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger

included.title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation

inclusion_criteria: text-based medical abstention, selective prediction, or uncertainty calibration
evaluation governance, claim/evidence provenance, or pre-registration
limitations: Not a systematic review; coverage is limited to the listed free sources and queries
Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were not queried
Forward and backward citation chasing from MedQAbstain, Med-PRM, MedAgentBench, FHIR-AgentBench, and BioClinical ModernBERT was not performed
Screening was performed by a single AI implementation agent without independent human double screening; a human pre-submission check is still required
arXiv preprints are not peer reviewed and are cited as preprints
Result sets reflect source relevance ranking on the search date
model_or_protocol_change: none; the refresh changes no model, threshold, calibration, benchmark, denominator, or result

novelty_disposition.candidate_claim: study-level contribution: one frozen-protocol evaluation of a compact non-generative clinical decision layer that reports null, negative, blocked, and calibration-pathology outcomes with every exported claim mechanically bound to source-hashed evidence packets
novelty_disposition.permitted_wording: This study reports a frozen-protocol evaluation in which every exported claim is bound to source-hashed evidence packets and null, negative, and blocked outcomes are reported. We do not claim methodological novelty for abstention, typed decisions, pre-registration, or provenance verification individually.
novelty_disposition.scope: Describes this study only; never phrased as first, as a novel method, or as state of the art.
